content: This medication has the potential to cause significant mental or mood changes, which may worsen during treatment or even after the last dose has been administered. It can also suppress your immune system, reducing your ability to fight infections. This suppression may increase your susceptibility to serious, and in rare cases, fatal infections, or exacerbate any pre-existing infections. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you are in the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, contact your doctor for guidance. Before using peginterferon alfa-2a, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, polyethylene glycol (PEG), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication may increase your risk of developing infections or worsen existing ones. Avoid close contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Notify your healthcare provider that you are using peginterferon alfa-2a before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. This drug may cause dizziness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can intensify this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication, particularly mental or mood changes, such as severe depression or suicidal thoughts or attempts. Peginterferon alfa-2a may also slow a child’s growth, potentially resulting in a lower-than-expected final adult height. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your doctor. You should not become pregnant while using peginterferon alfa-2a, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable birth control methods with your healthcare provider while on this medication. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as blood counts, thyroid tests, virus levels, kidney and liver function tests, triglyceride levels, and eye exams, should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically during its use. Do not switch brands of interferon without consulting your doctor or pharmacist. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember, provided it is within two days of the scheduled dose. Administer your next dose on the usual day. Store this medication in the refrigerator, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze it. Do not leave it out of the refrigerator for more than 24 hours. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
